subject: Literacy
title: Naming things around us
objectives: Children will name familiar people, foods and objects.
Children will say a word or two to ask for something.
content: Naming family, people, food and classroom objects, and using two words to ask for something.
teachingActivities: Use real objects first and pictures second; name each item before asking for it; extend single words into two words, such as "more rice"; celebrate every word.
learnerActivities: Name familiar people, foods and objects, and use two words together to ask for something.
resources: Real foods or toy foods: rice, bread, banana, water
Classroom objects: chair, table, cup, ball
assessment: Observe whether each child names at least ten things and uses two words together to ask.
expectedOutcomes: Names at least ten familiar things.
Uses two words together to ask for something.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: family and community

lessons.title: Family and people
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will name familiar people in a family picture.
successCriteria: Names or points to mummy, daddy and baby
Says a person’s name or a word for them
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals and pictures in books and say a few words with gestures.
resources: A family picture with mummy, daddy, baby and grandma
Family photographs from home if available
lessons.starter: Show the family picture and say "This is mummy. This is daddy. This is baby." Point to each.
teacherActivities: Point to each person and say the name. Ask "Who is this?"
Show a photograph and ask "Who is this?"
Let each child hold a picture and show it to a friend.
learnerActivities: Children point and say the name.
Child points to the baby.
Child says "mummy" or "grandma".
Child shows the picture and says the word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Point to each person and say the name. Ask "Who is this?" Children: Children point and say the name.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Where is baby?" and wait. Children: Child points to the baby.
Step 3. Teacher: Show a photograph and ask "Who is this?" Children: Child says "mummy" or "grandma".
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child hold a picture and show it to a friend. Children: Child shows the picture and says the word.

practical.title: My family
steps: Put family pictures on the mat.
Each child points to mummy, daddy and baby.
The group says the names together.
practical.safety: Handle photographs gently and return them at the end of the day. Be sensitive to children who live with relatives or one parent.

differentiation.support: Point together and say the word before the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name more people, such as uncle and aunty.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the family pictures.
lessons.homeConnection: Look at family photographs together and name each person.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name familiar people in a family picture" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Mummy, daddy, baby, me. We are a family.

lessons.title: Food we eat
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will name foods they eat and say a word to ask for them.
successCriteria: Asks for a food with a word or phrase
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals and pictures in books and say a few words with gestures.
resources: Toy foods or real washed fruit: rice, bread, banana, water
lessons.starter: Put the foods on a tray and say "Look! Rice, bread, banana." Ask "What do you like?"
teacherActivities: Hold up each food and say its name clearly.
Say "I want rice, please." Pretend to eat it.
Hold two foods and ask "Rice or bread?"
Let each child pick a food from the tray.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children copy "rice, please".
Child points or says the food name.
Child names the food and says please.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up each food and say its name clearly. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "I want rice, please." Pretend to eat it. Children: Children copy "rice, please".
Step 3. Teacher: Hold two foods and ask "Rice or bread?" Children: Child points or says the food name.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick a food from the tray. Children: Child names the food and says please.

practical.title: Pretend snack
steps: Set up a pretend snack table with toy foods.
Each child asks for a food by name.
practical.safety: Use toy foods or check allergies before any real food is shared. Wash hands first and keep real food for supervised snack time only.

differentiation.support: Offer two foods and say the name with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name three foods they eat at home.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you want?
questions.expected: A food name with or without please.

lessons.conclusion: Put the foods away and say "Thank you for the food."
lessons.homeConnection: Name the foods at mealtime and ask your child "What do you want?"
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name foods they eat and say a word to ask for them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Things in our classroom
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will name objects in the classroom.
successCriteria: Points to a chair, a table, a cup and a ball
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals and pictures in books and say a few words with gestures.
resources: A chair, a table, a cup and a ball
lessons.starter: Walk around the classroom and touch a chair. Say "This is a chair." Ask "What is this?"
teacherActivities: Walk around and name each object and let children touch it.
Say "Bring me the ball" and wait.
Hide an object under the cloth and ask "What is it?"
Let each child name an object and show a friend.
learnerActivities: Children touch and say the name.
Child brings the ball.
Child feels or guesses and names it.
Child shows the object and says the word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Walk around and name each object and let children touch it. Children: Children touch and say the name.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Bring me the ball" and wait. Children: Child brings the ball.
Step 3. Teacher: Hide an object under the cloth and ask "What is it?" Children: Child feels or guesses and names it.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child name an object and show a friend. Children: Child shows the object and says the word.

practical.title: Classroom treasure hunt
steps: Ask each child to find one when you name it.
Bring them to the mat and name them together.
practical.safety: Make sure the objects are light and safe to carry. Keep the floor clear and supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child and point to the object.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two objects when you name them.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you bring me the cup?

lessons.conclusion: Return each object to its place and say its name.
lessons.homeConnection: Name things at home and ask your child to fetch one by name.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name objects in the classroom" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Two words together
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will use two words together to ask for something.
successCriteria: Says "more rice" or a similar phrase
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals and pictures in books and say a few words with gestures.
lessons.starter: Hold a plate and say "More rice, please." Ask the children "What do you want?"
teacherActivities: Model the phrases "more rice", "my cup" and "big ball".
Hold out the plate and wait for the child to ask.
Give the item and say "Here you are." Wait for thank you.
Let each child be the shopkeeper and serve a friend.
learnerActivities: Children repeat the phrases.
Child says "more rice" or "rice, please".
Child says thank you.
Child serves and the friend asks.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Model the phrases "more rice", "my cup" and "big ball". Children: Children repeat the phrases.
Step 2. Teacher: Hold out the plate and wait for the child to ask. Children: Child says "more rice" or "rice, please".
Step 3. Teacher: Give the item and say "Here you are." Wait for thank you. Children: Child says thank you.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child be the shopkeeper and serve a friend. Children: Child serves and the friend asks.

practical.title: Pretend shop
steps: Set up a pretend shop with toy foods.
The customer asks with two words.
The shopkeeper serves and the customer says thank you.
practical.safety: Use toy foods and cups only. Keep the area clear and supervise turn-taking.

differentiation.support: Say the first word and wait for the child to add the second.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to ask for two things in a row.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you want?
questions.expected: A two-word request such as "more rice".

questions.question: What do you say after you get it?

lessons.conclusion: Close the shop and say goodbye to the customers.
lessons.homeConnection: At mealtimes, wait for your child to ask with two words such as "more water".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use two words together to ask for something" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 words check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how many words each child names and how they ask for things.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals and pictures in books and say a few words with gestures.
lessons.starter: Sing the "What is this?" song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: people, food and objects.
At each station ask "What is this?" and "What do you want?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child names the item and asks.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: people, food and objects. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is this?" and "What do you want?" Children: Child names the item and asks.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Words stations
practical.safety: Use toy foods and large pictures only. Supervise each station and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use real objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to name things for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names familiar things; uses two words together; asks with please.

questions.question: What do you want?
questions.expected: Child says a word or phrase.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
lessons.homeConnection: Name things at home and ask your child to ask for them with two words.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how many words each child names and how they ask for things" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
